sentences.text: Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 11762/2024 Pushpendra S/o Mangi Lal, Aged About 29 Years, R/o Asoda Banswara, Dist. Banswara.
----Petitioner Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Devendra Sanwalot For Respondent(s) : Mr. Dhanraj Vaishnav, Public Prosecutor JUSTICE DINESH MEHTA Order 12/11/2024 1.

This application for anticipatory bail under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.') has been filed by the applicant apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR No. 42/2023, registered at Police Station Hathipole, District Udaipur for the offences under sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC').

2. Mr. Devendra Sanwalot, learned counsel for the applicant argued that the allegations leveled against the applicant is that he has produced a forged mark-sheet at the time of the document verification.
3. Learned counsel submitted that going by the contents of the FIR, it is not the applicant who had prepared the mark-sheet.
He [2024:RJ-JD:45627] (2 of 2) [CRLMB-11762/2024] maintained that as a bonafide student, the applicant had procured such degree/certificate.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
5. Having regard to the contents of the FIR and the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant indulgence to the applicant.

Even if the facts narrated in the FIR are taken to be correct, so far as the applicant who has used the forged mark-sheet is concerned, may be held guilty of an offence punishable under section 471 of the Indian Penal Code.

6. Such being the position, in the case after the investigation, the Investigating Officer finds that an offence under section 471 of the Indian Penal Code has been committed by the applicant, the Investigating Officer shall issue a notice under section 41-A of the Cr.P.C.
7.
The bail application stands disposed of accordingly.
